card.title: Net force
card.body: The **net force** ($\sum\vec{F}$ or $\vec{F}_{\text{net}}$) is the single **vector sum** of all external forces acting on an object: $\sum\vec{F} = \vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2 + \dots$. In two dimensions, sum components along each axis ($\sum F_x$ and $\sum F_y$), then $|\sum\vec{F}| = \sqrt{(\sum F_x)^2 + (\sum F_y)^2}$.
card.says: combine every force on the object into one equivalent force; if they cancel to zero, the forces are balanced.
card.from: the principle of superposition of forces — multiple simultaneous forces produce the same effect as their single vector sum.
card.useWhen: two or more forces act on the same object and you need to decide whether it is in equilibrium ($\sum\vec{F} = \vec{0}$) or find its acceleration.
card.example: Pull a box with $15\text{ N}$ east, $9\text{ N}$ west, and $8\text{ N}$ north: $\sum F_x = 15 - 9 = 6\text{ N}$ east and $\sum F_y = 8\text{ N}$ north, so $|\sum\vec{F}| = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\text{ N}$.
card.analogy: In a game of tug-of-war, the rope responds only to the difference between the two teams' pulls — not to how hard each side strains individually.
